content: Hello! how can I help today?
Can I withdraw money from a 529 plan to pay for my child’s college housing?
Yes—room and board are qualified expenses if your child is enrolled **at least half-time**. The amount must not exceed the school’s published cost of attendance for housing.
Do I need to pay tax on the withdrawal?
If it’s used for qualified expenses—tuition, fees, housing, books—there’s **no tax**. Non-qualified withdrawals may trigger income tax and a 10% penalty on the earnings portion.
Can I use it for off-campus rent?
Yes, but only up to the amount the school includes in its **room and board allowance**. Save receipts and cross-check with the school’s official COA figures.
How do I report the withdrawal?
You’ll receive **Form 1099-Q**. As long as withdrawals match qualified expenses, you don’t include them on your return. But keep detailed records in case the IRS questions it.
